keywords.meaning: as expected; after all; on second thought
keywords.nuance: Used when reality matches an expectation, when you return to an earlier opinion, or when you change your mind after considering something.
keywords.example: やっぱり日本語は面白い。
keywords.exampleTranslation: Japanese really is interesting after all.

keywords.nuance: Shows that something is done carefully, responsibly, completely, or in the expected way. It often carries the feeling of ‘not carelessly.’
keywords.example: 毎日ちゃんと勉強しています。

keywords.nuance: Most commonly used with a negative form to soften a statement: あまり分からない means ‘I don’t understand very well.’ In positive sentences, it can also mean ‘too much,’ but that usage is less basic.
keywords.example: アニメはあまり見ません。
keywords.exampleTranslation: I don’t watch anime very much.

keywords.nuance: Often expresses that the degree is higher than expected. Depending on context, 結構です can also mean ‘No, thank you’ or ‘That is fine.’
keywords.example: この本は結構難しいです。

questions.prompt: やっぱり、この店のラーメンが一番おいしい。
questions.hint: The speaker’s experience confirms what they already believed.
questions.answer: As expected, this restaurant’s ramen is the best. / This restaurant’s ramen really is the best after all.

questions.prompt: 宿題をちゃんとやりましたか？
questions.hint: The question is asking whether the homework was done properly or completely.
questions.answer: Did you do your homework properly? / Did you actually finish your homework?

questions.prompt: 昨日はあまり眠れませんでした。
questions.hint: あまり is paired with a negative verb here.
questions.answer: I couldn’t sleep very well last night. / I didn’t get much sleep last night.

questions.prompt: 今日は結構暑いですね。
questions.hint: The heat is stronger than the speaker may have expected.
questions.answer: It’s quite hot today, isn’t it?
